alerts.reason: Reported sales moved from -7.65% year over year in March to -4.86% in June. I forecast the September quarter stays narrowly above -5.00% and the December quarter crosses back to -5.00% or lower. The timing is uncertain because the June improvement left only 0.14 percentage points of clearance.

Reported sales improved from -5.70% year over year in March to -4.944% in June. I forecast September stays just above -5.00%, consistent with the 4% full-year sales decline (B). Lower sales and production volumes (E) leave little room for further weakness before a December crossing.

June net sales fell 1.6%, an improvement from March's 7.01% decline. Lower volume cost $9.38 million in June sales, while price increases added $2.44 million (A, C). I expect pricing to keep September above -5.00%, but forecast a December decline of at least 5% as volume losses outweigh that support.

Reported revenue moved from +0.14% year over year in March to -3.21% in June (B). Oilfield Services & Equipment lost $0.4 billion of revenue across international and North American markets, while Industrial & Energy Technology added $0.2 billion (A, C). I expect that growth to keep September above -5.00%, with the December decline reaching 5% if the oilfield losses widen.

June net sales fell 4.4%, but the order backlog fell 28.3%, or $150.3 million, year over year (A, C). I forecast existing orders keep September sales above -5.00%, then the smaller pool of orders available to ship pushes December sales to -5.00% or lower.

Reported revenue improved from -4.50% year over year in March to -2.65% in June, supporting a September forecast above -5.00%. Consumables and activity-based equipment accounted for about 80% of first-half revenue, and the global rig count fell 6.2% year over year in June's quarter (A, C). I forecast a December crossing as reduced drilling activity feeds through to orders.

Reported revenue fell 3.11% year over year in March and 1.64% in June. Subscription and services growth of $264.7 million supports a September forecast above -5.00% (A, B). Lower bitcoin trading volume already outweighed the benefit of higher bitcoin prices (D). I forecast a December crossing if that volume loss deepens enough to overwhelm services growth.

The year-over-year decline narrowed from 11.60% in March to 3.25% in June, yet reported sales slipped from $2.104 billion to $2.091 billion. The improvement came from a lower prior-year comparison. I forecast September stays above -5.00% and December crosses back below it. The timing depends on the prior-year comparisons, which are unavailable for both quarters.

Revenue growth slowed from 15.10% year over year in March to 9.09% in June (A). The filing attributes a $6.7 million inventory increase to lower demand (B). The remaining growth supports a September forecast above -5.00%, while the inventory buildup points to weaker subsequent shipments and a possible December decline of at least 5%.

Revenue improved from -7.41% year over year in March to -1.01% in June (A). Stable truckload volumes extended into early September-quarter trading, but temporary customer capacity needs accounted for part of the fleet increase (B, C). I expect September to stay above -5.00% and forecast a December crossing as temporary loads fall away.

The reported revenue decline widened from 0.74% year over year in March to 2.74% in June. Extending that two-percentage-point deterioration per quarter gives approximately -4.74% in September and -6.74% in December. This numerical forecast puts the new crossing in December.

Reported revenue moved from +4.35% year over year in March to -0.74% in June (A). Daily LTL shipments fell 2.8%, while pricing and mix raised revenue per shipment excluding fuel surcharges by 2.7% (B, D). I expect pricing to cushion September enough to stay above -5.00%, then forecast a December crossing if shipment losses deepen.
